column1: # IPA -> speech backend tokens for planet/language/speak.py (audio lane, 2026-11-03). Reasoning: docs/review/language/audio.md.
# One row per base symbol, modifier or prefix. speak.py tokenizes an IPA string by longest match on the base rows, then takes the
# prefix rows before and the modifier rows after; every symbols.tsv row must tokenize fully (tests/test_language_speak.py).
# kind: base | mod (follows a base) | pre (precedes a base: prenasalization) | sep (word or syllable punctuation).
# espeak: eSpeak NG phoneme mnemonics, read inside [[ ]] with the 'hi' voice's phoneme table (base1 + consonants + Hindi:
#   it has nasal vowels, breathy and aspirated stops, retroflexes, long vowels). A mod's espeak value is appended to the base's.
# piper: IPA characters fed straight to a Piper voice's phoneme_id_map (en_US-lessac-medium: trained on English eSpeak IPA, so
#   sounds English lacks go to the nearest sound it was trained on). '-' = nothing (the sound comes from an effect or is dropped).
# fit: exact | near (a close sound the backend has) | sub (a different sound standing in) | effect (rendered in numpy afterwards).
# effect: what speak.py adds in post-processing on that segment's time span (click, percussive_lip, percussive_teeth,
#   percussive_beak, growl, purr, source2, sub, ultra, tone_<n>, breathy, creaky, ejective, implosive).

column7: piper: English has no retroflex stop
piper tʲ: no trained palatal stop; t + j glide
voiced uvular stop: no backend has it
trill: espeak 'r', piper flap (English has no trill)
piper: English has no ç; h before a front vowel is close
piper: nearest trained sound is h
pharyngeal approximant as a velar fricative
piper: ɬ is in the id map (Welsh names in English eSpeak)
piper: English l is dark anyway
implosives as plain voiced stops plus a short low-pitch dip
clicks: no backend speaks them; a glottal closure from the backend plus a synthesized click burst
lip smack: closure plus a soft low wet transient
teeth clack: closure plus a sharp bright transient
beak clap: closure plus a hollow mid-spectrum knock
no front rounded vowels in either (hi 'y' renders as silence)
piper ᵻ: English eSpeak's reduced high central vowel
hi lacks a short æ; ɛ is closest
aspiration: an h after the stop
breathy-voiced release (hi b# d# g#); piper h
ejective as stop + glottal stop, with a sharpened burst
piper: ʲ is in the id map
nasal vowel (hi a~ e~ i~ o~ u~); piper's combining tilde (French names in English eSpeak)
breathy voice: noise mixed into the segment
dental mark dropped (dentals rendered as alveolars)
tie bar (k͡p etc. are base rows; a stray tie is ignored)
tone letters: pitch set on the segment in numpy
VoQS harsh/ventricular phonation: ~80 Hz amplitude modulation plus noise
house second source: a second line a fifth up (its own contour from tone letters after ᴖ; speak.second_voice)
house sub-bass register: octave down plus a sub-bass rumble (the real one is below hearing)
house ultra register: octave up plus a faint high whistle (the real one is above hearing)
